study type: Comparative observational study and literature review
exposure: Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) with speech delay
Absence of autism and language disturbances
cohort: The study included 6 preschool children with early childhood autism and speech disorders, and 6 children without autism and language disturbances as a comparison group.
finding: Children with normal speech development exhibited bilateral symmetric activation of the superior temporal gyri, while children with autism showed lateralized and limited involvement of the auditory cortex.
